title: Captain Quorum and the Motion to Adjourn
author: Civic Morale Directorate (uncredited)
blurb: A pre-Collapse civic title about a man whose superpower is procedure. Printed on paper better than anything made since, in flat confident colours, by an office that wanted you to feel a very particular way about committees. Read now, it is either the funniest thing in the shop or the most frightening, and the shop’s proprietor will not tell you which.
source: Scanned from the Mint Condition reading copy, Ironside Street, Coldwater. In-universe fiction.

chapters.title: Part One: A Point of Order
chapters.text:
A civic hall, in the clean confident line of a studio with a deadline and no opinions. Bunting. A raised dais. Two hundred citizens in the seats, and not one of them has a face. It was a budget decision. Eighty years later it does the work for free.

On the dais: CAPTAIN QUORUM. Sash, cape, gavel. Square jaw. Municipal green and municipal gold.

CAPTAIN QUORUM: Friends! Neighbours! Ratepayers!
CROWD: HOORAY!

CAPTAIN QUORUM: The Directorate has proposed a THIRD RESERVOIR for our growing city!
CROWD: HOORAY!

A figure stands up in the third row. He has a face. He is the only person in the issue apart from Quorum who has one, and it is a weaselly face, and he is coloured in a sour purple that appears nowhere else on the page.

DISSENTER: And who's paying for it?

The crowd turns. Two hundred blank ovals, all rotated fifteen degrees.

> A hush fell over the hall. For into every civic process, sooner or later, there comes... A POINT OF ORDER!

---

Quorum raises the gavel. Speed lines. A small starburst. It is a superhero panel about a man raising a gavel and there is no way around that.

CAPTAIN QUORUM: I recognise the gentleman!
DISSENTER: I said WHO'S PAYING
CAPTAIN QUORUM: The gentleman is RECOGNISED, and the gentleman has THREE MINUTES!

A clock appears in the corner of the panel. It stays in the corner of every panel for the next nine pages.

DISSENTER: My family has drawn water from the Marrow cut for four generations

> 2:41

DISSENTER: and now they tell us the cut is to be capped, and the reservoir is to be METERED, and a METER is to be fitted in every KITCHEN

> 2:09

Quorum in the foreground, back to us, gavel resting on his shoulder like a bat. Perfectly relaxed.

> 1:52

---

DISSENTER: and I say, I SAY, that a city that measures its people will one day BILL them for existing, and I say the reservoir is not a gift, it is a LEDGER, and I say

> 0:14

The dissenter stops. He looks at the clock.

He looks at the two hundred blank ovals.

> 0:00

Quorum turns around. Big grin. All teeth.

CAPTAIN QUORUM: Thank you! The gentleman's time has expired! The gentleman may submit the remainder IN WRITING!
CROWD: HOORAY!

---

The dissenter sits down.

The dissenter is still sitting down.

The chair beside him is empty and we did not see anybody leave.

Quorum, arms spread, cape out, the whole hall behind him.

CAPTAIN QUORUM: THE MOTION CARRIES!
CROWD: HOORAY!

> And so, thanks to the tireless vigilance of CAPTAIN QUORUM, the business of the city was CONCLUDED, in FORTY-ONE MINUTES!

> A NEW RECORD!

chapters.title: Part Two: The Motion to Adjourn
chapters.text:
A back room. Smaller, browner, no bunting. Three figures at a table, all blank-faced, all in the same municipal green.

DIRECTORATE OFFICIAL: Captain, the gentleman submitted in writing.
CAPTAIN QUORUM: Splendid! The system WORKS!

A document is slid across the table. We see it side-on. It is very thick.

DIRECTORATE OFFICIAL: He submitted four hundred pages.
CAPTAIN QUORUM: Ah.

Close on Quorum. The first time in the issue his jaw is not square.

DIRECTORATE OFFICIAL: Under Standing Order Eleven, a written submission must be READ INTO THE RECORD.
DIRECTORATE OFFICIAL: In FULL.
DIRECTORATE OFFICIAL: By the CHAIR.

Quorum, magnificently, straightens his sash.

CAPTAIN QUORUM: Then I shall read.

---

The hall. Empty seats. One figure on the dais, reading aloud.

> He read for six hours.

The same view. The light through the high windows has moved.

> He read for eleven.

The same view. Dark outside. A lamp on the lectern.

> He read for nineteen.

The same view. Light again.

> The Standing Orders did not provide for a recess. This was not an oversight. Captain Quorum had drafted them himself, in a happier year, and he had been very proud of that clause, and he had explained it to a great many people at a great many functions.

---

Close. His voice is drawn as a thin wavering balloon line, the one the studio kept for radios and for the dying.

CAPTAIN QUORUM: "and I say that a city that measures its people will one day bill them for existing"
CAPTAIN QUORUM: "and I say the reservoir is not a gift, it is a ledger"

He stops. He is looking at the page.

The page. We see it. It is the same paragraph again.

He turns over. It is the same paragraph again.

He turns over. It is the same paragraph again.

---

Four hundred pages, fanned across the dais floor. Every one identical.

CAPTAIN QUORUM: ... he only wrote it once.

Wide, from the back of the hall. One small green figure alone on a dais, surrounded by paper, in a building with nobody in it.

CAPTAIN QUORUM: He only wrote it once and I have said it four hundred times.

The doors at the back of the hall. Shut.

The gavel, on the lectern, where he has put it down.

---

He picks it up.

He raises it.

The gavel comes down across the whole page, speed lines, starburst, the entire apparatus of a superhero landing a blow, and the caption in the same cheerful municipal lettering as every caption in the book:

> "The Chair moves that this meeting be ADJOURNED."

> There being no objection,

> and there being nobody present to object,

> the motion CARRIES.

---

The empty hall.

The empty hall.

The empty hall, and on the far wall, low, half-hidden behind a stack of folded chairs, a small painted-over cabinet with a little glass window.

> NEXT MONTH: CAPTAIN QUORUM in "A FRIENDLY AMENDMENT"!

> Ask your newsagent to reserve your copy!

---

> On the inside back cover: CIVIC MORALE DIRECTORATE. Printed by authority. Not to be sold above the cover price. Not to be defaced. Not to be retained after the period of currency.
